Source: Javier Villalba's public Kaggle notebook jvillalba007/unitree-rl-mimic (kaggle kernels output), which itself checks out unitreerobotics/unitree_rl_mjlab (MuJoCo/IsaacLab-family, NOT unitree_rl_gym/IsaacGym like this repo's own g1/g1_deepmimic tasks) as its training framework. INCOMPATIBLE AS-IS with this repo's g1_deepmimic task: onnx input 'obs' is [1, 154] (mjlab's own single-frame obs convention), while g1_deepmimic's own num_observations is 1380 (frame_stack=5 x (151 proprioceptive + 125 ref-motion features), see g1_deepmimic_config.py). This is a hard dimension mismatch, not just a semantic one (see the distinction the rugiar skill draws for 'stable') -- rugiar_driver.py will refuse it for --task g1_deepmimic, and rugiar distill would refuse it as a teacher too (check_dimensions_compatible() checks obs dims). 'task' below is intentionally NOT any currently-registered task name, so this stays discoverable (rugiar train --list_policies) without a driver ever trying to auto-load it into a mismatched env. Making it usable needs either a new task registered with mjlab's own 154-dim obs pipeline, or running Javier's own mjlab sim to extract a motion trajectory (same treatment as the g1-moves clip already converted) rather than reusing these weights directly. See docs/motion_imitation_integration.md.
